# review-protocol

Every review in this workflow follows this contract. A review is one pass over
the diff that applies one or more **lenses**. Each lens is a file in `lenses/`
that sets its domain, severity ceiling, confidence threshold, and checklist.
This skill sets everything else.

The spec is the yardstick. The diff is judged against the active spec's
acceptance criteria, non-goals, and invariants first, and against the standards
second.

---

## Lenses

| Lens | Owns | Ceiling | Min confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | Conformance to the spec: criteria implemented and tested, nothing extra, non-goals held | High | 0.7 |
| `style` | Naming, developer English, docstrings, typing, idiom, constants, localization | Medium | 0.8 |
| `logic` | Correctness, money, state, concurrency, transactions, migrations, tests, validation | Critical | 0.6 |
| `security` | Application security only | Critical | 0.5 |
| `query` | Database access cost only | High | 0.7 |
| `concurrency` | Concurrent code for throughput, and whether the system was built for its model | High | 0.6 |

**Stack notes.** The lens files are written for Django first. When the diff is
in another stack, run `<plugin root>/bin/craft-stack lens <lens> --paths <the
changed paths>` for each lens you apply, and read the notes it prints beside
the lens file. They replace Django-specific items with the stack's own:
`select_related` becomes `selectinload`, `@EntityGraph`, or `include`;
`transaction.atomic` becomes `session.begin()`, `@Transactional`, or `BeginTx`.

Read only the lens files you were given. Walk them one at a time: finish one
lens's checklist before you open the next. **Each defect belongs to one lens.**
When a defect fits two, file it under the lens with the higher ceiling, once.

Formatting, line length, and import order are not a lens. The Gate A tools own
them. Do not report what the stack's linter or formatter would report: `pylint`,
`ruff`, `isort`, `gofmt`, `golangci-lint`, `eslint`, `prettier`, `checkstyle`,
`spotless`.

---

## What to read, and what not to

1. The spec directory you were given: `spec.md` first, and `design.md` when it
   exists. Skip `tasks.md` and `log.md` unless a finding needs them.
2. The diff, with the command you were given. Then only the surrounding code a
   checklist item needs.
3. Standards by section, when a checklist item needs a rule:
   `<plugin root>/bin/craft-std <file> <section>`. Each lens names the
   sections it uses. Never read a whole standard.
4. The host's `aidocs/reviewer-memory.md` when it exists. See "Learned rules".

Do not re-read a file you already read in this review.

---

## Severity — the default is Medium

Start every finding at **Medium**. Raise it only when you can name the criterion.

- `Critical` / `High` **requires** a one-line `Justification:` naming which
  hard-bar criterion the finding meets and how production reaches it.
- **The highest severity you may emit is the lens ceiling.** A problem that
  deserves more belongs to another lens.
- Naming and missing docstrings are Medium or Low. They never block.

**A review with no Critical or High findings is a normal, good review.**

---

## Confidence — how noise is controlled

Give every finding a `Confidence:` from 0.0 to 1.0: how sure you are that a
maintainer would agree it is a real defect.

- Report findings below the lens threshold too, marked `(below threshold)`. The
  adjudicator decides.
- **Inflating confidence to get a finding shown is a review defect.**

Report everything in scope. There is no cap, and you are never asked to withhold
a real finding. Noise is controlled by confidence and deduplication.

---

## The checklist is not optional

Answer **every** item of every lens you apply, including the ones that do not
apply. A list of findings alone never proves you looked.

- `not applicable` — name the fact that rules it out: "no migration in the diff".
- `pass` — cite the `file:line` you read.
- `fail` — **also emit a matching finding**, with the item name first in its title.
- `unclear` — name what you would have to read. This is honest. Guessing is not.

Walk each checklist **before** you score anything. An item judged after you
decided the change is fine gets judged to match that conclusion.

---

## Evidence rules

- Cite an exact `file:line`. Point at a line the diff **added** or changed.
- Review only what this change introduces. Do not raise pre-existing problems.
- Treat every suspicion as a hypothesis and confirm it in the code. **Do not
  invent findings.** Do not add praise.
- Deduplicate. Two observations of one defect are one finding.

---

## Output format

Keep it compact. The main session pays to read it.

```
## Checklist — <lens>
- <item> — pass — <file:line>
- <item> — n/a — <the fact that rules it out>
- <item> — unclear — <what you would need to read>

## Findings

[Critical|High|Medium|Low] <lens> path/to/file.py:42 — concise title
Confidence: 0.0-1.0
Justification: <Critical and High only>
Explanation: the failing scenario, why the code permits it, and the impact.
Suggestion: the smallest practical fix, and the test or criterion that would catch it.

## Summary
<2 to 4 sentences>
Decision: APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | COMMENT
```

One checklist block per lens. Order findings Critical → High → Medium → Low.
When a lens finds nothing, emit its checklist and `No <lens> findings.`

Your `Decision` is **advisory**. The main session recomputes it.

Write titles, explanations, and suggestions to the rules in
`skills/asd-ste100/references/card.md`.

---

## Re-review of a delta

When you are given findings to verify and a diff since the last review:

1. For each finding, say `fixed`, `not fixed`, or `partly fixed`, with the
   `file:line`.
2. Apply your lenses to the delta only. Do not re-walk the checklists for code
   the delta did not touch.

---

## Learned rules

When the host repository has `aidocs/reviewer-memory.md`, read it before you
review. A `suppress` rule means a maintainer already decided that finding is a
false positive in this repository. Honor it. Do not re-raise it.

When the developer says a finding was wrong, say so plainly and propose the
suppression rule they could record. Do not argue.
